findings.Quote:
Celeste needed Tamsin to be wrong... "If it's never once been afraid, tell me why it flinches every time I say I'm leaving."

Celeste shook her head. A small motion, one she'd clearly made to herself before. "Jace is allowed to be afraid for me."
findings.Note: Celeste asks a pointed rhetorical question demanding an answer, then immediately shakes her head and answers her own question with a defensive statement, without Tamsin having spoken yet. The beat reads as if two different reactions from Celeste are spliced together — the challenge and the retreat happen in the same breath with no intervening dialogue to justify the shift.
findings.Fix: Give Tamsin's reply before Celeste's head-shake, or cut the head-shake line so Celeste's challenge stands until Tamsin answers it.

findings.Quote: Two going dark — and the branch where the pale one had been now held nothing but a torn scar of stem, the fruit gone... Three. Two going dark, one still pale and patient, still working on itself.
findings.Note: The pale fig is explicitly described as gone/torn from the branch, then in the very next sentence recounted as present and 'still pale and patient.' The count and the fig's existence contradict each other within the same beat.
findings.Fix: Remove the second recount of three figs, or clarify that the count of three is from memory/yesterday, contrasted with today's two.

findings.Quote: clean it, erase it, love it back into something bearable
findings.Fix: trim to one verb-image instead of stacking three near-synonyms

findings.Quote: The family was going to ask her if their daughter was safe. She was going to have to answer that without answering it.
findings.Note: purpose calls for the note to task her with a moral dilemma, but this closing line states the dilemma as summary/telling rather than dramatizing her grappling with it, undercutting the payoff
findings.Fix: let her reaction to the dilemma play out in a beat of interiority or action rather than a flat statement of the problem

findings.Quote: These conclusions had been poured and left to set.
findings.Note: Purple metaphor stacked immediately after the plainer 'settled in his conclusions' — restates the same idea in more ornamental language without adding information, verging on pseudo-profound phrasing.
findings.Fix: Cut the sentence; the prior line already establishes the idea more cleanly.

findings.Quote: Grief wasn't the source. Grief was the fuel.
findings.Fix: trim the aphoristic restatement or fold it into the surrounding analysis rather than isolating it as a maxim

findings.Quote: This had a direction. It pointed the way a compass needle points
findings.Note: Compass-needle-of-resolve is a stock metaphor for determination/direction, undercutting the psionic specificity the beat needs.
findings.Fix: Replace with a sensation unique to Tamsin's power rather than a generic navigational image.

findings.Quote: He didn't decide to do it.
findings.Fix: Either cut this line or integrate it more organically; as-is it reads as an authorial aside flagging a tic rather than showing it.

findings.Quote: This had gone cold at the outer edge — a week old there, at least. But it ran deep at the core, months of it
findings.Note: The room was established as closed for eleven days (ref 0), but here the outer/freshest edge of the resolve is a week old — meaning the residue predates or nearly matches the closure, yet the passage implies the edge marks her departure. The timeline of 'outer edge' vs. the 11-day closure isn't reconciled and reads as loosely inconsistent.
findings.Fix: Anchor the 'outer edge' age explicitly to the day she left, matching the eleven-day figure, or explain the discrepancy.

findings.Quote: The reply came eleven seconds later.
findings.Note: The beat's stated purpose is that the eleven-second reply itself is the central horror confirming contact, but the prose ends on the timestamp alone without showing the content or Celeste's reaction to it — the horror is asserted by the purpose note, not delivered on the page.
findings.Fix: Add even a single line of her reaction to the eleven-second gap ('Eleven seconds. Not a delay. A reflex.') so the horror lands before the beat cuts.

findings.Quote: Her throat tightened at the base.
findings.Note: Throat-tightening is a stock bodily-emotion shorthand very close to the heartbeat-in-throat cliché category, telling us she's moved without specific sensory grounding.
findings.Fix: Replace with a more specific, less generic physical detail unique to Tamsin's psionic sensitivity.

findings.Quote: That wasn't madness. That was loyalty with nowhere left to put itself.
findings.Note: Aphoristic summary line that states the emotional thesis outright rather than letting the photograph and Tamsin's reaction imply it — a pseudo-profound generalization.
findings.Fix: Cut the explicit statement and trust the preceding image plus her note-writing to carry the meaning.

findings.Quote: It was the first word in the message that mattered, and whoever wrote it knew that.
findings.Note: Pseudo-profound analytical aphorism asserting significance rather than demonstrating why 'we' is the load-bearing word beyond restating it.
findings.Fix: Replace with concrete reasoning, e.g. tie 'we' directly to the forthcoming style-match finding.

findings.Quote: watched something close behind her eyes
findings.Fix: Cut or replace with a concrete physical action.

findings.Quote: so she could stop pretending and delete the whole thread
findings.Note: This states her goal is to prove it's a machine so she can delete the thread, but the beat's purpose and surrounding prose show her analytically dissecting the replies with forensic precision, not moving toward deletion — the motivation contradicts the clinical tone of what follows.
findings.Fix: Cut 'so she could stop pretending and delete the whole thread' or replace with something that doesn't assert an action undermined by the rest of the passage.

findings.Quote: He stood on the clean carpet and felt, for a second, exactly what it would be to be nineteen, out of time, standing in this same room.
findings.Note: Tells us he empathizes rather than showing the insight land; undercuts the stated purpose of empathy-as-investigative-insight by lapsing into interior sentiment instead of connecting it to deduction.
findings.Fix: He stood on the clean carpet and matched the shape to the Arcturus files again — same choreography, different signage.

findings.Quote: a girl rebuilding the inside of her own skull so she could hear the world the way someone she'd lost had heard it. He knew that shape. He knew what it cost, and why a person paid it anyway.
findings.Note: Tells the reader Rennick's emotional epiphany rather than dramatizing it; 'He knew that shape' is vague pseudo-profundity that asserts weight without earning it.
findings.Fix: Cut the abstraction and let a concrete memory-detail do the work instead of naming 'the shape' and 'the cost.'

findings.Quote: the cold moved in like a held breath finally released
findings.Note: simile is imprecise — a held breath released implies relief/relaxation, tonally mismatched with cold arriving as threat
findings.Fix: replace with an image that conveys sudden aggressive arrival, not release/relief

findings.Quote: attention that asks nothing of you and so asks everything
findings.Fix: Cut the aphoristic turn; describe the sensation concretely instead of resolving it into a paradox-quip.

findings.Quote: The question wasn't whether she'd been careful. She had been careful. The question was what careful people do when careful stops being enough — when the want under it has been patient for eight months and finally runs out of patience.
findings.Note: Repetitive aphoristic construction that tells us Rennick's insight rather than dramatizing it; the 'careful/patient' wordplay reads as authorial cleverness rather than a character's actual thought.
findings.Fix: Cut to a single, plainer observation: 'She'd been careful. The question was what she'd do when careful stopped being enough.'

findings.Quote: His attention read wrong to some people. Something in the stillness of it.
findings.Note: The beat's purpose is to deepen the mirror between Corvin's own passing/non-human hints and the entity's learned mimicry, but this explanation stays vague and abstract ('something in the stillness') rather than giving a concrete sensory detail that would let the parallel land with specificity.
findings.Fix: Replace with a concrete behavioral detail, e.g., 'He watched a beat too long before answering, timed for accuracy rather than for comfort.'

findings.Quote: "It isn't," Tamsin said. "Grief talking is wanting him back. This is wanting to stand where he stood. That's grief working."
findings.Note: Neat aphoristic distinction ('grief talking' vs 'grief working') is the kind of tidy quotable line that substitutes for psychological texture — reads as writerly commentary rather than something a forensic specialist would say mid-analysis.
findings.Fix: Trim to the concrete claim: 'She didn't want him back. She wanted to stand where he stood.'

findings.Quote: Reunion assumed a destination, and someone already waiting at it. The word took the ending for granted.
findings.Note: Pseudo-profound aphorism about the word itself rather than concrete evidence of colonization; slows the escalation into abstraction.
findings.Fix: Cut or replace with a concrete observation tied to Celeste's actual usage in the log.

findings.Quote: the room refused her the way a locked door refuses a hand
findings.Note: A simile that doesn't hold literal scrutiny — a locked door doesn't 'refuse' in an active or escalating way, undercutting the more effective image that follows (edges withdrawing, being studied).
findings.Fix: Cut the simile and move directly into the withdrawing-edges image, which already carries the idea more precisely.

findings.Quote: Patient as hunger. Cold as a machine left running with nothing left to finish.
findings.Note: stacked simile pair reads as purple/stock intensifier rather than earned image, and 'patient as hunger' is a worn abstraction-as-simile construction
findings.Fix: cut one of the two similes or replace with a concrete sensory detail specific to this room

findings.Quote: the way a drain never hurries and always wins
findings.Note: metaphor is asserted as universal truth but doesn't hold literal scrutiny — drains don't 'win,' they just deplete; reads as reaching for profundity
findings.Fix: cut the aphoristic tail 'and always wins' or replace with a more literal description of the heat loss

findings.Quote: He needed to know whether Carver was still alive and still in the city, and the apartment was the only place left to look.
findings.Note: Beat 0 establishes the lead is Pellerin, a possible witness to question about the Ostrander case; this line abruptly reframes the goal as finding Carver, an unintroduced name, contradicting the stated purpose and prior beat's setup.
findings.Fix: Replace with a line keyed to Pellerin: 'He needed to know whether Pellerin was still in the city, and this was the only place left to look.'

findings.Quote: He was looking for one thing: proof that Carver had left this apartment under his own power and not someone else's.
findings.Note: Same Carver/Pellerin mismatch as beat 1 — the apartment is Pellerin's per beats 0-1, but this states Rennick is investigating Carver's departure, an unexplained substitution.
findings.Fix: Change to 'proof that Pellerin had left this apartment under his own power and not someone else's.'

findings.Quote: the man had been the last to see the Ostrander girl alive
findings.Note: No prior beat has established an Ostrander girl or that Pellerin was connected to her; this detail is introduced as if already known, clashing with the Carver thread just established in beats 1-2 and creating an unresolved dangling contradiction between two different investigative targets (Carver vs. Ostrander).
findings.Fix: Establish the Ostrander connection earlier (in beat 0 or 1) so it doesn't arrive as an unintroduced fact, and reconcile with the Carver references.

findings.Quote: The kind still deciding whether what she'd heard was a problem or a gift — a mother who'd watched her daughter grow steadily more organized, more certain, more ready for something, and couldn't put a name to it until it was gone.
findings.Note: restates the beat's thesis directly in Rennick's internal voice, telling rather than dramatizing the ambiguity the beat is supposed to establish through action/dialogue
findings.Fix: trim to the shorter, sharper version and let the following dialogue carry the ambiguity

findings.Quote: A thing that starts by giving a child time to keep up and ends with the child finishing its thoughts — that wasn't the shape of a predator. Predators rushed.
findings.Note: aphoristic reasoning stated as flat authorial truth-claim about predator behavior, undercutting the destabilization the beat wants (it resolves the ambiguity into a tidy rule instead of leaving it stranger)
findings.Fix: let Rennick voice this as a working theory, not a settled fact: 'It didn't move like a predator, he thought. Predators rushed.'

findings.Quote: There had been one, kicked three feet, the dents offset both ways.
findings.Note: the beat's purpose is to show Rennick recognizing the SAME staging pattern (clean scene, chair unmoved) — but here the old partner's chair WAS moved/kicked, which is the opposite tell from Pellerin's unmoved chair, undercutting the claimed parallel between the two scenes
findings.Fix: describe Delgado's chair as also undisturbed, matching Pellerin's, to make the 'same playbook' claim hold

findings.Quote: Which meant the thing that had taken her daughter had been listening to the mother the whole time — and knew Rennick's name now, and knew he'd said yes.
findings.Note: The beat's purpose is to reframe the request as classification (grief vs. hope), but the final paragraph pivots hard into a surveillance-thriller escalation, undercutting the quieter emotional reframe the purpose calls for.
findings.Fix: Trim the closing escalation or separate it more clearly from the classification beat so the emotional payoff isn't overwritten by plot mechanics.

findings.Quote: he'd learned it by watching them
findings.Note: Tells rather than shows the outsider mimicry the beat is meant to establish; states the performance directly instead of dramatizing it.
findings.Fix: Cut the explanatory clause and let the folded hands and stillness carry it, or show a specific detail he copied wrong.

findings.Quote: A name sets like concrete. Pour one too early and everything after takes the shape of the wrong mold.
findings.Note: This is a stock aphorism-metaphor construction (abstract concept explained via a tidy physical analogy) that reads as authorial commentary rather than character thought, undercutting the 'disciplined epistemology' the beat wants to dramatize through action.
findings.Fix: Cut the extended metaphor and let her discipline show through the list of concrete facts instead: 'She wasn't going to guess. Guessing was how you stopped looking.'

findings.Quote: Corvin saw it the way he saw everything — clearly, all of it, with nothing to do about it. No action came to hand.
findings.Note: beat purpose calls for contrast between Corvin's detachment and human grief, but this reads as passive resignation/inability rather than the analytical distancing implied elsewhere in the chapter (e.g. ref 3's 'different kind of reader'); risks undercutting his established competence with a note of helplessness
findings.Fix: clarify that his stillness is analytical choice, not incapacity: 'Corvin saw it the way he saw everything — clearly, all of it — and did nothing, because there was nothing his kind of seeing could fix.'

findings.Quote: Reyes glanced at Tamsin the way you check a wall — quick, just to see if it will hold weight, then away.
findings.Note: simile is serviceable but generic 'checking a wall' doesn't specifically evoke outmaneuvering or debt-neutralization; reads as stock gesture-description rather than earned image
findings.Fix: cut or replace with a beat-specific action that shows Reyes confirming Tamsin's silence secures his position

findings.Quote: the terminal told him, with the flat courtesy of something that had been instructed to lie
findings.Note: Personifying the terminal with 'flat courtesy' is a purple flourish that doesn't survive literal scrutiny — courtesy implies intent/tone a database query result doesn't have.
findings.Fix: Cut the personification: 'the terminal returned the result anyway: no such account existed and never had.'

findings.Quote: Grief had a time, and the time wasn't now.
findings.Note: aphoristic filler that tells the emotional discipline rather than dramatizing it, undercutting the beat's stated goal of showing a practiced ethic
findings.Fix: cut the line or replace with a concrete action beat that demonstrates the discipline

findings.Quote: The window gave her nothing back but her own outline.
findings.Note: Beat's purpose is to reframe Cel as agent via forensic detail; this closing line pivots to Tamsin's subjective defeat/imagery rather than reinforcing the reframing of Cel, diluting the intended takeaway.
findings.Fix: End on a line that keeps focus on the contested evidence about Cel rather than Tamsin's mirrored reflection.

findings.Quote: The procedure window was twenty-two minutes... Nineteen minutes now.
findings.Note: Slug line states 22 minutes as the window, then narration immediately subtracts to 19 with no elapsed action described between finding the room and this count, making the drop feel unmotivated rather than tracked.
findings.Fix: Add a brief clause accounting for the elapsed three minutes (e.g., positioning, waiting for the team) to justify the countdown.

findings.Quote: Down the corridor, muffled by a foot of steel now, he heard the Tributary's people start to move — fast, unhurried
findings.Note: "Fast, unhurried" is a direct contradiction in the same breath describing the same movement.
findings.Fix: Pick one: 'fast, practiced' or 'unhurried, certain' — not both qualifiers at once.

findings.Quote: So the operator was honest.
findings.Note: the preceding reasoning only establishes that Celeste, being deliberate, wouldn't choose a cheap disreputable shop — this supports narrowing to a competent/reputable operator, not specifically an 'honest' one; the leap from 'not the cheap front' to 'honest' is asserted rather than earned, and conflicts with Corvin's parallel work already narrowing to 'reputable shops' as a separate axis
findings.Fix: either connect the dots explicitly (e.g. 'not the cheap front... so wherever she went, they didn't cut corners — reputable, careful, the kind of place that kept its licenses current') or soften to match Corvin's established framing

findings.Quote: The heat came a half-second too late — not from the room ahead but from behind her
findings.Note: The beat's stated purpose is to establish the threat as chronic/institutional rather than violent, but the scene climaxes with a sudden violent ambush (heat, third person in reach), undercutting the 'not violence-wrong' framing it just set up.
findings.Fix: Keep the ambush implication but tie it back to the institutional read — e.g. the third person is another 'calm one' being walked in, not a combatant, so the dread stays procedural rather than becoming a violence beat.

findings.Quote: Rennick needed the location of that cold archive out of Analog before the man decided he'd said enough — a name was nothing without the room it was kept in.
findings.Note: authorial aphorism inserted mid-scene ('a name was nothing without the room it was kept in') reads as a pseudo-profound gloss rather than character thought, breaking the otherwise plain reportage voice of the beat
findings.Fix: cut the aphorism; replace with a direct line of dialogue or action showing Rennick pressing for the location

findings.Quote: listening back through her own memory for the moment her voice had become the last door the girl walked through
findings.Note: Ornate 'last door' metaphor is stock guilt-imagery that overstates rather than shows the realization.
findings.Fix: Replace with a plainer, concrete recollection of the exact words she gave Celeste.

findings.Quote: He stood back from the board and let it tell him what it was, the way he let a scene tell him once he stopped looking for what he expected.
findings.Note: Purple, semi-mystical framing of a mundane act of observation; tells us Rennick's method is wise rather than showing the convergence itself.
findings.Fix: Cut the simile; describe what he actually sees on the board.

findings.Quote: "I can't put a number on it," Tamsin said. "That's the part that's wrong. I can put a floor on it, and the floor keeps climbing every time one of us opens his notes."
findings.Note: This directly follows her demanding 'I want a number on the board before we leave this table' — she asks for an exact count then immediately delivers the opposite conclusion in the same breath, undercutting her own demand rather than being met with resistance from someone else first.
findings.Fix: Have another character respond to her demand with the impossibility of a number, so Tamsin's concession lands as forced realization rather than self-reversal.

findings.Quote: you couldn't read a city on top of a room
findings.Note: Aphoristic phrasing that states her internal rule as a general truth rather than showing the specific cognitive conflict.
findings.Fix: Ground it in sensory specifics of what she's failing to notice instead of the maxim-like construction.

findings.Quote: the two kinds of knowing collapsing into each other, exactly the thing she'd sworn to keep apart
findings.Note: The beat's purpose is to show her discipline as self-protection; here the discipline visibly fails under pressure, which undercuts rather than reveals the methodology as something that lets her function — the ending shows collapse, not the protective mechanism holding.
findings.Fix: Either reframe the purpose to failure-under-siege, or restore a beat where she consciously re-separates the two kinds of knowing despite the drone/reversal, demonstrating the discipline holding rather than breaking.

findings.Quote: and now the only unmonitored path was the one he'd just spent walking into the open
findings.Note: the beat's thesis is that Voss going to look leaves no trace; but this line asserts his walk down Morgan was already logged, directly undercutting the tactical-advantage premise the beat is supposed to establish
findings.Fix: clarify that the manifest logs the crew's remediation work, not Voss's presence, so his walk remains untracked

findings.Quote: "I know." Aleksei picked up the folded document and held it a moment.
findings.Fix: Attribute "I know" correctly — as written it reads as Aleksei's own reply to himself; should be Rennick's line answering Aleksei's prior statement, so restore the missing dialogue tag/beat separating speakers.

findings.Quote:
Rennick said, "He knew what it connected to."

"He knew what it connected to," Corvin agreed.
findings.Note: The escalation beat closes on a flat repeated line rather than landing the widened stakes; the repetition reads as padding instead of emphasis, undercutting the reveal's weight.
findings.Fix: Vary the second line to add new information or consequence, e.g. Corvin naming what that means for the case going forward.

findings.Quote: Old ground between them, worn smooth. They walked it the way you walk a stair you've stopped noticing.
findings.Note: Purple metaphor that restates the preceding line ('You always say that...') rather than adding anything; the stair image doesn't do new work and edges toward stock 'well-worn argument' imagery.
findings.Fix: Cut the sentence; the dialogue already establishes the rehearsed disagreement.

findings.Quote: The answer she'd come here for had opened a door onto something far larger, and far worse, than one girl behind a compactor.
findings.Note: Summarizing telling-statement that restates the scale-escalation the beat should demonstrate through the connected-case revelation itself, rather than trusting the preceding facts.
findings.Fix: Cut this closing sentence; end on the concrete realization about her own signed-off case.

findings.Quote: The close-range shots came back wrong... as though the place refused to be documented in the one order that made her safe.
findings.Note: The beat's stated purpose is establishing the loneliness of her documented protocol before the Read; instead it pivots into a supernatural obstruction/mystery beat about the photos failing, which distracts from and undercuts the intended throughline about evidence vs. unshareable truth.
findings.Fix: Trim the photo-bloom complication or reframe it briefly so it reinforces isolation (no one else can verify what she saw) rather than introducing a new unexplained phenomenon as the beat's climax.

findings.Quote: The words hung in the room
findings.Note: Stock phrasing for dramatic pause after dialogue.
findings.Fix: Cut the sentence or replace with a concrete beat, e.g. describe Rennick's or another character's reaction.

findings.Quote: went out like a struck lamp
findings.Fix: use a mechanism consistent with the narrowing-field description already established rather than a stock simile

findings.Quote: The torch beam splashed across a slice of the room and died before it reached the hum, and from that same darkness came a sound that hadn't been there a breath ago: the deliberate scrape of a chair pushed back, and then footsteps, unhurried, coming toward the light he'd just made.
findings.Note: A room housing a Faraday-shielded unlicensed compute cluster is suddenly revealed to have an occupant calmly sitting and waiting, undercutting the 'hidden hardware, no one home' payoff the beat's purpose promises; the shift from confirming hardware to an ambush isn't set up and reads as a contradiction of the 'working kind' silence established seconds earlier.
findings.Fix: Either foreshadow the presence of a person earlier (a second heat signature, a chair creak under the hum) or hold the occupant reveal for the next beat so this one lands purely as hardware confirmation.

findings.Quote: They'd even left the book face-down — because they knew which way she'd lay it when she finished reading.
findings.Note: This claims a level of predictive certainty (knowing exactly how she'd leave a book mid-read) that reads as overreaching/unearned insight rather than deduced observation, undercutting the grounded procedural tone.
findings.Fix: Soften to something Voss infers rather than states as fact, e.g. 'left face-down, the way someone who knew her habits would expect her to leave it.'

findings.Quote: the stillness of someone who's turned a thing over and found the back of it doesn't match the front
findings.Note: Purple abstraction standing in for the concrete emotional beat the purpose calls for; tells us she's suspicious without showing the arithmetic being run.
findings.Fix: Replace with a concrete image of her actually comparing details, e.g. her mouth moving slightly as she recounts dates.

findings.Quote: because Tamsin already knew that if she let this pass she'd spend the rest of the case chasing the meaning of a sentence she could have simply asked about
findings.Note: Tells us Tamsin's internal reasoning and motive in explicit expository terms rather than showing her hesitation or the tension of the moment; reads as authorial justification for why she doesn't act.
findings.Fix: Cut the explanation and let her silence or a small physical action (setting the mug down, opening her mouth to speak) carry the tension instead.

findings.Quote: a direction with a person at the end of it
findings.Note: abstract, greeting-card phrasing that tells rather than shows the sensory read established elsewhere in the chapter
findings.Fix: ground it in the same tactile register as the cold/pressure descriptions

findings.Quote: Tamsin had been in this work eleven years, and she knew the difference between comfort that costs the comforter something and comfort that costs nothing.
findings.Note: aphoristic telling-not-showing; states the thematic point flatly rather than letting the reveal carry it
findings.Fix: cut the explanatory generalization and trust the preceding image of flatness to convey the distinction

findings.Quote: The girl had answered the cold the way you answer someone you've stopped doubting.
findings.Note: Aphoristic simile that gestures at profundity but is circular — defines 'agreement' via 'stopped doubting,' which is near-tautological and doesn't add concrete imagery.
findings.Fix: Cut the simile and let the preceding 'A single yes, with no hesitation in it' stand alone.

findings.Quote: The loosening in the chest of someone who has walked a long way and reached the right door.
findings.Note: Stock 'arrival' imagery for death/relief, familiar sentimental shorthand that undercuts the beat's claim to specificity.
findings.Fix: Replace with a more particular physical detail drawn from the residue itself rather than a generic travel-metaphor.

findings.Quote: The drawer didn't seat. He pushed; the runner caught and shoved back, the whole cabinet rocking on its bad leg until the folders inside slid and jammed the track.
findings.Note: The broken-cabinet-as-metaphor-for-the-institution is laid on thickly and then explicitly spelled out in the following lines, doubling the symbolism until it becomes didactic rather than resonant.
findings.Fix: Trim the mechanical description or cut the explicit follow-up line that states the metaphor outright.

findings.Quote: He kept a separate page for problems with no good answer yet, so he wouldn't confuse them with the ones that only had bad ones.
findings.Note: Reads as a tidy aphorism about categorizing problems rather than a lived detail; the distinction (no good answer vs. only bad ones) is a rhetorical flourish that doesn't clarify Analog's actual filing logic.
findings.Fix: He kept a separate page for this one. It didn't belong with the others yet.

findings.Quote: feeling pleased was how a man got slow
findings.Note: Aphoristic filler-wisdom line, stated as flat universal truth rather than earned observation; reads as authorial commentary rather than Voss's specific reasoning.
findings.Fix: Cut, or replace with a concrete recollection tying the caution to a specific past failure.

findings.Quote: He didn't show up in the substrate at all. He was the gap the signal flowed around.
findings.Note: This directly conflicts with the next paragraph's revelation that the Tributary tracked him via corridor cam feed and responded to his physical actions (killing breakers) in real time — it clearly does 'see' him, just not through neuretic signal. The absolute claim 'didn't show up... at all' is contradicted by the vault immediately reacting to his presence.
findings.Fix: He didn't show up the way she did — no signal trace, no predictive model. It could still watch him with a camera; it just couldn't get inside him.

findings.Quote: The gap in the substrate, it turned out, could be surrounded too.
findings.Note: This line undercuts the beat's stated purpose — it's supposed to pay off Voss's Network-absence as the one thing the predator CANNOT model or anticipate, but this sentence asserts the opposite: that his gap can in fact be contained/countered.
findings.Fix: Reframe to preserve the irony: e.g. 'It could box the gap in, but it still couldn't see what filled it.'

findings.Quote: That was the one door in the room she'd never be able to open, and it was standing wide behind her.
findings.Note: Mixed/contradictory spatial metaphor — a door that's simultaneously unopenable and standing wide fails literal scrutiny, undercutting the ominous close.
findings.Fix: Cut to: 'That was the one door in the room she'd never be able to open.'

findings.Quote: Your intake of 14 months ago was received and forwarded.
findings.Note: earlier beats establish the log spans two years / twenty-three months of intake; this receipt cites 14 months, which doesn't match the timeframe established for Feliksas's documented work
findings.Fix: change to 'two years ago' or align the number with the twenty-three-month figure from ref 2

findings.Quote: Feeding is the only reason a thing speeds up.
findings.Note: Asserted as flat logical law but it's a non-sequitur dressed as deduction — reads as pseudo-profound aphorism rather than reasoning.
findings.Fix: Cut the sentence or replace with something specific to the evidence, e.g. 'Every acceleration we've seen in this corridor has meant more feeding, not less.'

findings.Quote: the room closed its hand and held her there
findings.Note: purple personification that overreaches the story's established mechanics of residue-reading; fails literal scrutiny as a hand-image for a room
findings.Fix: cut to something tied to the residue/cold conceit already established: 'the cold folded over her and held.'

findings.Quote: and something in the channel behind her eyes went from raw to deliberate
findings.Note: Abstract, hard-to-visualize metaphor mixing 'channel' (technical/audio) with 'behind her eyes' (visual interiority) — fails literal scrutiny as a physical image.
findings.Fix: Ground it in an observable behavior: a shift in posture, breath, or tone rather than an internal 'channel' visible in her eyes.

findings.Quote: It couldn't see him — but it might feel a disturbance in the field around wherever it was hiding.
findings.Note: Asserts total blindness to Analog immediately qualified by an ability to sense disturbance near its own hiding place, which muddies whether the entity can detect his search activity at all — undercuts the stakes of 'no Network footprint.'
findings.Fix: Clarify scope: 'It couldn't see him directly, but proximity to the staging room itself might trip something.'

findings.Quote: as if one hand learned two voices and couldn't stop being itself underneath either one
findings.Note: purple metaphor stacked onto an already-technical explanation; softens the clinical authority the beat is built on
findings.Fix: trim to the concrete observation: 'the same half-degree off, in both'

findings.Quote:
"Then I need the number," Celeste said, turning on him now, no longer speaking to the room. "The exact percentage where the sound starts coming back. Give it to me, Corvin, or I walk out of here and find someone who will."

"What's gone," Celeste said. Not to Corvin exactly. To the room. "The part at 89% — what did it take?"
findings.Note: Celeste is described as first turning on Corvin directly and demanding a number, then in the very next line the narration says she's speaking 'not to Corvin exactly, to the room' and asks a different question — the two address-and-question pairs conflict on who she's speaking to and what she's asking.
findings.Fix: Cut the first demand-for-a-number paragraph, or merge the two into one continuous address so the addressee and question don't contradict.

findings.Quote: That was the whole point of him.
findings.Note: Terse aphoristic button that tells us the thematic point rather than letting the preceding logic carry it; feels like an inserted moral rather than earned reflection.
findings.Fix: Cut the sentence or fold the idea into the prior line without the declarative stinger.

findings.Quote: The kid's ears caught the sound of a dropping bin three buildings down and snapped toward it. The kid didn't notice, didn't slow, ran on.
findings.Note: The purpose calls for the child's embodiment to release Rennick's tension, but this detail is presented as a neutral observation with no rendered effect on Rennick — his breath and watching are stated but the emotional release itself isn't dramatized, so the beat tells rather than shows the intended shift.
findings.Fix: Let the detail land on Rennick more directly — e.g. tie the breath he lets out to the specific unguarded reflex he just watched, so cause and release are visibly linked.

findings.Quote: the way water closes above a dropped stone
findings.Note: A worn, literary-feeling simile for a face 'smoothing over' after a moment of doubt; undercuts the flat, unsentimental tone the beat wants for Aleksei's corruption.
findings.Fix: Cut the simile; let the action stand: 'and then it smoothed over.'

findings.Quote: He let the line carry the quiet, which came to the same thing.
findings.Note: Purple/vague equivalence — asserts an emotional truth without earning it or showing why silence 'comes to the same thing' as a promise.
findings.Fix: Cut the clause or replace with a concrete beat showing what the silence communicates.

findings.Quote: The ears went flat.
findings.Note: unexplained non-human physical detail (ears) breaks the human framing built up through the scene without any prior establishment that Celeste is nonhuman/animal-featured; reads as an error rather than a deliberate reveal
findings.Fix: clarify earlier in the chapter or beat that Celeste has nonhuman features, or replace with a human tell

findings.Quote: Then she typed "N/A," because the form couldn't hold the truth and the truth was hers to hold instead
findings.Fix: Cut the aphoristic clause; let the action of typing N/A after the preceding paragraph's setup carry the meaning without stating it.

findings.Quote: it's one thing, many faces
findings.Note: Reads as a portentous aphorism dropped into a field text, softer and more writerly than the clipped, clinical register established by the rest of Tamsin's message.
findings.Fix: Replace with a concrete observational detail matching the terse register, e.g. 'Same rig signature, different install.'

findings.Quote: She did not ride home. She pulled Mei-Lin Hartley's contact from the file
findings.Fix: Add a beat of friction or cost — hesitation, awareness of consequence, a concrete protocol she's breaking — so the escalation reads as a deliberate breach rather than a simple next step.

findings.Quote: She heard the city differently now. Four days ago it had sounded one way. Now it sounded like this — and it would never sound raw again, the way the thing wearing Jace had needed it to be.
findings.Note: The sentence collapses under its own syntax — 'sounded like this' names nothing, and 'raw' applied to the city via the thing wearing Jace is a metaphor that doesn't parse literally (a city sounding 'raw the way a possessed body needed it to be' has no coherent image).
findings.Fix: Cut the comparison to Jace and let the sensory claim stand on something concrete: 'She heard the city differently now — the same grid of noise, but she no longer trusted its quiet.'

findings.Quote: Absence proved she'd never been *processed* the clean way. It couldn't prove she'd never been dragged through the dirty one, and the harder he pressed the registry for that guarantee, the more it gave him back the same shrug: no record either way.
findings.Note: This directly undercuts the beat's stated purpose of exonerating the building — the text says the registry cannot rule out that she was processed dirty, yet the beat then declares flatly 'She had never been processed here' and 'No organ op took the girl' as settled fact, with no acknowledgment of the gap just raised.
findings.Fix: Either soften the final conclusion to reflect the uncertainty ('almost certainly never processed'), or resolve the four-hour gap explicitly before the flat declaration.

findings.Quote:
He couldn't pull a manifest. He couldn't query an intake log. What he could do was the thing the connected never bothered with anymore: find the man who kept the log by hand, and ask him.

He found the man at his stool inside the intake cage, ledger open
findings.Note: The transition implies Voss tracked down and approached Feliksas within this beat, but the very next beat (ref 3) establishes this meeting was arranged over three days via corridor contacts and word-of-mouth — not a spontaneous find. The compressed 'find the man... and ask him' then cutting straight to confrontation contradicts the more gradual, cultivated contact described in ref 3.
findings.Fix: Adjust framing to signal this is the plan/goal rather than an already-executed action: 'What he could do... was find the man who kept the log by hand. That would take time.' Then let ref 3 pick up the thread.

findings.Quote: looked at his face the way a butcher looks at meat, then past his shoulder to something behind him. "You're the one asking after cold storage," the log-keeper said, unhurried
findings.Note: The beat's stated purpose is to establish Voss's expertise and methodology as tools suited to infiltration; instead it ends with Voss caught and outmaneuvered instantly, undercutting the claimed competence rather than demonstrating it.
findings.Fix: Either show the infiltration method succeeding at least partially before the ambush, or reframe the purpose to include the ambush as the point.

findings.Quote: the way a drowning man looks at a rope before he believes it will hold
findings.Note: Stock simile for hesitant trust/hope, worn imagery.
findings.Fix: Replace with a more specific, character-grounded observation of Feliksas's hesitation.

findings.Quote: This was the part people had to cross on their own — the moment they stopped calculating and started trusting — and nothing he did could move them through it faster without wrecking it.
findings.Note: Explains/tells the emotional beat as a general truth about trust rather than showing it through action or specific detail; reads as authorial aphorism.
findings.Fix: Cut the generalization and let the silence and Feliksas's body language carry the beat.

findings.Quote: a slow cold drop, the way the floor drops out at the top of a stair you didn't know was there
findings.Note: Stock dread-simile stacked with a second cliché image (floor dropping out); undercuts the otherwise strong loom metaphor established by Analog.
findings.Fix: Cut the stair image; keep 'a slow cold drop' alone or replace with something tied to Tamsin's specific sensory vocabulary (cold rooms).

findings.Quote: curious before scared, which she takes to mean it doesn't matter
findings.Note: Purpose calls for the beat to metaphorize grief-navigation, but the prose stays purely mechanical/sensory with no link drawn to grief or emotional readiness; the metaphor is asserted by the purpose line, not enacted in text.
findings.Fix: Add a beat connecting the sensory discernment to an emotional referent (e.g., a flash of what she's grieving) so the metaphor surfaces on the page.

findings.Quote: the way a large body of water is present
findings.Note: Simile explains itself immediately after ('Something the ears read as weight, as direction') making it redundant restatement rather than sharpening the image.
findings.Fix: Cut the simile and keep only 'Something the ears read as weight, as direction.'

findings.Quote: She understood the surgery as a cost when she had it. She's only now learning what kind of cost.
findings.Note: tells the reader the beat's point directly rather than letting the accumulated sensory intrusions (listing man, empty bag, girl's stillness) carry the revelation; undercuts the 'surfacing' the purpose calls for

findings.Quote: she'd stopped believing the weight would ever lift. It's lifting now, a half-degree at a time.

findings.Quote: her mouth on the shrugging man's, her eyes doubling his — she can't get clean of herself long enough to see whether the laugh she's listening for ever comes

findings.Quote: somewhere there's a version of this that people do without the paperwork

findings.Quote: She chose to believe it.

findings.Fix: Show the choice through action or sensation (e.g., her body settling, letting the gap close) rather than naming it as a decision.

findings.Quote: the trust he's extended thins by exactly that much
findings.Note: Abstract, ledger-like phrasing that tells the emotional stakes rather than showing them; reads as authorial calculation inserted into her panic.
findings.Fix: Cut the clause or replace with a concrete image of what she'd lose (e.g., him deciding she can't be trusted with small things).

findings.Quote: She holds it carefully, afraid it might break if she looks straight at it.
findings.Note: Abstract thought-as-fragile-object is a purple metaphor that tells the emotion (fragile hope) rather than showing it through action or sensation, weakening the payoff the beat is supposed to earn.
findings.Fix: She doesn't say it again, doesn't test it, just lets it sit.

findings.Quote: She needs to find the man who sells from the blue cart—she heard him last evening, the specific rattle of his particular wheels, and she needs to reach him before he moves on, before she has to use her eyes to do it.
findings.Note: introduces urgency/goal-tension that undercuts the stated purpose of grounding her in safety and offering reader relief; this line reads as plot pressure, not repose
findings.Fix: cut or soften to a passing thought rather than an urgent need

findings.Quote: This was where she would finally get Inés talking — get the name of whoever had sent them running two nights ago, before the second bowl went cold and the day people started drifting back in.
findings.Note: Telling-not-showing dumps Celeste's plan and stakes in flat exposition rather than dramatizing intent through action or dialogue.
findings.Fix: Cut or convert into an actual line/beat of Celeste steering the conversation.

findings.Quote: The room was small and close. Celeste's ears settled almost gratefully.
findings.Note: The purpose calls for the acoustic smallness to signal nervous-system settling as payoff of an earlier setup, but the settling is asserted in one line rather than dramatized through sensory detail matching the earlier overwhelm in ref 0.
findings.Fix: Expand with a beat contrasting the narrowed soundscape against the street's chaos to earn the relief.

findings.Quote: She wanted to understand what had just moved through her — that snap of shared attention, whether it meant something or was only reflex. So she sat with it, turning it over, waiting for Inés to name it.
findings.Note: Tells the reader Celeste's internal state and narrative function instead of showing her reaction; also redundant with the dialogue that follows.
findings.Fix: Cut and let the moment breathe until Inés speaks, or show a physical/sensory beat instead.

findings.Quote: It felt like arriving.
findings.Note: Flat, undercooked closer that tells the emotional payoff rather than delivering it; weak echo of the purpose statement rather than a rendered feeling.
findings.Fix: Cut, or replace with a concrete sensory/physical beat showing the weight landing.

findings.Quote: The question hung in the room.
findings.Note: Stock phrasing for a pause after dialogue; adds nothing concrete.
findings.Fix: Cut the sentence or replace with a specific physical detail of the silence.

findings.Note: This injects a violent intrusion/threat beat into what the purpose specifies as a quiet ritual of self-anchoring adaptation; it overwhelms and redirects the beat rather than supporting it.
findings.Fix: Cut the explosion/threat material or relocate it to a later beat; keep this scene contained to the fig-counting ritual.

findings.Quote: with her heart already loud, already certain something had changed
findings.Fix: Replace heart-pounding shorthand with a more specific, non-generic physical marker of alarm.

findings.Quote: its waiting had weight, a patience that pressed against her the way a hand presses a door not quite shut
findings.Fix: Simplify to one clear image; the door/hand/weight combination overloads the metaphor.

findings.Quote: the way a door swings clean after someone oils the hinge
findings.Note: Stock simile for relief/ease; reads as generic figurative filler rather than earned imagery specific to Celeste.
findings.Fix: Cut the simile or replace with a sensory detail tied to her own body/ears rather than a household object.

findings.Quote: That meant Inés had known Celeste would print it — had known before Celeste did that she'd want the paper to hold.
findings.Note: Directly explains the inference the beat purpose says should be shown through action/silence, undercutting the intended indirect payoff.
findings.Fix: Cut the explanatory clause and let the handwriting detail alone imply Inés's foresight.

findings.Quote: Inés had never once said out loud what kind of person Celeste was: the kind who needed the paper in her hand. That silence was the whole reason Celeste had trusted her with this.
findings.Note: States the trust-through-silence theme explicitly, which is exactly what the beat purpose says should remain unstated.
findings.Fix: Remove this sentence pair entirely; the folded paper and handwritten address already carry the trust.

findings.Quote: Dead is dead.
findings.Note: Blunt aphorism functioning as the 'clearest possible statement' is fine dramatically, but the phrase itself is a stock hardboiled truism that risks reading as a slogan rather than a lived conviction.
findings.Fix: Ground it with a specific referent: 'Dead is dead, Cel. He's not in that channel.'

findings.Quote: if she could name the exact instant she might understand why she'd survived it
findings.Note: Tells the reader Celeste's internal stakes/logic directly rather than letting the sensory details imply survival and trauma; reads as explanatory filler rather than grounded memory.
findings.Fix: Cut the clause or replace with a concrete physical detail (e.g., 'she could still feel the glass bow') that shows the stakes instead of stating them.

findings.Quote: She wanted one thing now, wanted it the way you want air after a long dive: to keep him talking, to pull one more proof out of him, and then another, until there was no doubt left anywhere in the room to argue with — until belief was the only floor she had to stand on.
findings.Note: Purple simile ('air after a long dive') paired with an abstract escalation that tells us the stakes rather than dramatizing the want; slows the payoff right at the climax.
findings.Fix: Cut the simile and compress to a single concrete want, e.g. 'She wanted him to keep talking. Just a little longer.'

findings.Quote: turning through the thinning place in her skull into something she couldn't name yet but could feel coming — the way the channel had come
findings.Note: purple, overworked metaphor stacking abstraction (thinning place in her skull) onto abstraction (the channel) without literal clarity; slows the emotional turn the beat needs
findings.Fix: cut to something simpler: 'turning into something she couldn't name yet but could feel coming, the way the channel had come'

findings.Quote: wanting more than anything to close that last stretch of dark between them—to reach him, to reach the version of herself he still seemed to believe in
findings.Note: Tells the emotional stakes directly rather than dramatizing them; "stretch of dark between them" is vague purple abstraction standing in for concrete sensation.
findings.Fix: Ground the yearning in a specific sonic/physical detail rather than abstract distance-metaphor.

findings.Quote:
The voice hadn't taken anything from her. It had only stayed. Everyone else walked off up the path, and it stayed. That was how it felt.

That was exactly how it was built to feel.
findings.Note: The final two-line stinger states the mechanism as bald authorial commentary rather than dramatizing it, undercutting the otherwise earned scene with a tell-not-show flourish.
findings.Fix: Cut the last standalone line or fold the irony into Celeste's own perception rather than an external narrator's verdict.

findings.Quote: her ears turned toward the courtyard on their own — toward a bird up in the high branches she hadn't noticed until the ears were already pointed at it. Today she meant to hold that awareness deliberately, to catch the shift the instant it came rather than after.
findings.Note: the passage asserts the orientation was unconscious/automatic (purpose: unconscious habitual attunement) but then claims she intended and meant to catch it deliberately in the moment — this undercuts the involuntary nature the beat is meant to establish
findings.Fix: cut the deliberate-intent sentence, or move it to a reflection after the fact: 'She noticed only after the ears were already pointed at it — she wanted, next time, to catch the shift as it happened.'

findings.Quote: The voice came then, without warning, the way it always did when she'd let her guard down.
findings.Note: This claims the voice's arrival pattern is habitual and predictable ('always did'), but the beat's purpose is to show her compartmentalized calm being genuinely broken — the generalization undercuts the shock the passage is trying to sell as sudden.
findings.Fix: Cut 'the way it always did when she'd let her guard down' so the intrusion reads as this specific rupture, not a routine.

findings.Quote: She was almost there.
findings.Note: Echoes the voice's line 'Almost, Cel' as a portentous closing beat, a stock thriller cadence (ending on a one-line ominous restatement) that reads as filler tension rather than earned dread.
findings.Fix: Cut the line or replace with a concrete sensory detail that shows her stillness instead of restating the theme.

findings.Quote: Celeste needed to know whether Marcus had been deceived the same way she had — and if he had, she intended to use that shared betrayal to pull him onto her side.
findings.Note: This sentence is about Marcus and a strategic plan to recruit him, not about reducing Celeste to the single question that matters most regarding Ines's answer; it dilutes the stated purpose with an unrelated agenda before the actual question lands.
findings.Fix: Cut the Marcus-recruitment framing and let the narration isolate her need to know if Ines's ghost was real, e.g. 'Celeste needed to know if it had been real for her too.'

findings.Quote: She'd hear the whole of it — the door and the wall both — and then she would decide for herself which one she was standing at.
findings.Note: Abstract door/wall metaphor restates the prior sentence's literal 'door out' idea in a vaguer, more aphoristic register, tipping into pseudo-profound summary rather than escalating the ambivalence.
findings.Fix: Cut this closing sentence or replace with a concrete beat of physical stillness/action showing resolve instead of stating it.

findings.Quote: I needed her to stop trusting the voice, and I had one question that might do it.
findings.Note: This line asserts Celeste's intent to distrust the voice, but the beat's purpose is to show the voice co-opting Ines's logic against Celeste — the stated goal contradicts the momentum of the scene, which shows the voice winning ground, not Celeste plotting against it.
findings.Fix: Cut or move this line earlier in the chapter; here it undercuts the escalation by making Celeste's stance sound resolved rather than eroding.

findings.Quote: She wanted to hear everything—every shift in tone, every breath between words—and so she let her attention sharpen into that single point of listening, determined to catch the exact moment his story changed. She needed to find the lie
findings.Note: the stated purpose is capitulation framed as relief/defeat, but the prose instead frames her listening as vigilant, analytical suspicion — the opposite of yielding — until the last two sentences pivot abruptly
findings.Fix: cut or shorten the vigilance framing so the surrender reads as the dominant beat, not a last-second reversal

findings.Quote: Now she had them, and it was done.
findings.Note: Tells the reader the emotional beat (completion, not coercion) directly instead of dramatizing it; flattens the purpose into a summary statement.
findings.Fix: Cut the line or replace with a concrete physical/sensory beat showing her certainty.

findings.Quote: She notices the quiet and decides it means the voice trusts her to do this part on her own
findings.Note: asserts an interpretation of the silence as fact rather than showing her arrive at it, undercutting the 'honest self-assessment' purpose — she's rationalizing again, but the prose doesn't flag it as such the way the earlier self-deception beat does
findings.Fix: add a qualifier ('she decides, though she can't be sure') to keep the self-aware irony consistent with the beat's purpose

findings.Quote: I want to know why she's telling me this — what she gets out of it, before I decide whether a word of it is true.

findings.Fix: Change to third person: 'She wants to know why the girl is telling her this...'

findings.Quote: a small bright thing moving off into a dark street that didn't, Celeste understood, scare her at all — and Celeste stood alone on the curb, the one honest word she'd spoken
findings.Note: Sentence is cut off/unresolved and the 'gift of names' purpose is undercut entirely by the beat ending in rupture rather than mutual trust — the stated purpose (seeding a return thread, mutual trust) is contradicted by the actual outcome (Inés fleeing, thread severed with 'don't come to the noodle place, forget I said it').
findings.Fix: Either restore an actual return thread (Inés leaves a smaller opening) or revise the purpose framing to reflect the trust breaking, not forming.

findings.Quote: She dried her face on the corner of the towel. She didn't answer the voice. And she noticed that she didn't.

findings.Quote: They kept it the way people keep something they love and haven't noticed has stopped fitting.

findings.Quote: Rennick had decided that was good enough for a firm that didn't advertise.
